newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Porsche sees steady 96/97 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Porsche sees steady 96/97 profit.

text.p: German sports car maker Dr. Ing. h. c. f. Porsche AG on Tuesday reported a 40 percent jump in sales in the first quarter of its 1996/97 business year and said profit for the full year would at least match 1995/96.

Porsche also said the Boxster two-seat cabriolet -- its first new car in nearly two decades -- would push car sales and production up to 30,000 units in the year to July 31 1997 from around 20,000 in 1995/96.
Sales for the full year would rise to just over three billion marks ($1.9 billion) from 2.8 billion, Porsche said.
Management board chairman Wendelin Wiedeking acknowledged in a speech that his profit forecast was modest, partly because of continuing start-up costs for the Boxster.

"My slightly reserved attitude in making this forecast is attributable in particular to the expenditure we will still be incurring in this business year on the start-up of the Boxster, ongoing investments in future projects and further expenditure on markets," Wiedeking told a news conference.
In the 1995/96 year ended July 31, Porsche's net profit surged to 48 million marks from 2.1 million marks. That enabled the company to pay its first preferred dividend since 1991/1992, 2.50 marks.
In the first quarter of the current year, sales climbed 40 percent to 822 million marks due in large part to strong demand for its 911 model in the U.S., Porsche's largest car market, Wiedeking said.
Unit car sales climbed 55 percent during the period to 6,181 units.
"More than half of our sales of 911 models, that is exactly 3,192 cars, was in North Amercia, representing an increase by no less than 90 percent over the same period last year," Wiedeking said.
Wiedeking said that by the end of November production of Porsche's two models, the Boxster and the 911 was split 40-60. At the beginning of 1997 Porsche is aiming for a 50-50 balance of the two cars.
